page.overview:
Who is Skawn Bonduna?

Skawn Bonduna was a Twi'lek male celebrity and musician during the last years of the Galactic Republic. During the later reign of the Galactic Empire, he performed the lead role in the band Sonic Free, which rebelled against new Imperial laws on music. All members of the band were imprisoned, except for Bonduna, who gained a 30,000-credit bounty on his head. The Twi'lek then assumed aliases traveling the galaxy and earning low wages performing in cantinas, casinos, and cruise liners. At one point, Bonduna was identified aboard a luxury liner, causing word to spread about his appearance.

During the last years of the Galactic Republic, Skawn Bonduna was a celebrity rising in popularity. The teenager would occasionally appear in holovids and, at an early age, garnered success through popular recordings. Bonduna did not shirk the pursuit of knowledge and was academically successful, enough so that his test scores indicated he could have thrived as a governor or attorney. Bonduna was the lead performer in a band that went by the name Sonic Free, in which he and the other members used harmless subliminals in their music to uplift the moods of their listeners.

Bonduna and Sonic Free rebelled against the new Imperial laws that had their performances restricted and their recordings censored, causing the members to be charged by the Empire. The government body claimed that Sonic Free manipulated their innocent listeners with their words, allowing them to fall to Rebel Alliance propaganda and start revolting. By 9 BBY, all members of the band, save for Bonduna, who gained an Imperial bounty on his head, were arrested by the Empire and died in a prison brawl. Bonduna evaded capture and traveled across the galaxy under aliases. In the Outer Rim, the musician made low income performing in many second rate casinos, cantinas, and cruise liners.

At some point during the Empire's reign, Bonduna was discovered on a luxury liner that traveled too close to the Mid Rim for the performer's tastes. He denied that he was himself, but word spread of his discovery. Two weeks later, the information on the incident was made available by the Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations on the Imperial Posting DataCore database. At the time, he was marked for disintegration for a reward of 30,000 credits for anyone that held an Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificate.
